items.headline: India's June 2026 inflation rises to 4.38%, exceeding RBI target
items.summary: India's inflation increased to 4.38% in June 2026 from 3.93% in May, surpassing the RBI's 4% target due to supply-side and geopolitical factors. Analysts project CPI to average around 5% through H1 next fiscal year. RBI maintained repo rate at 5.25% in June. Bank of India revised MCLR rates, effective Aug 1, increasing 3-month to 8.35% and 1-year to 8.80%.

items.headline: Government interventions boost subsidies, structural reforms anticipated
items.summary: Government interventions helped contain inflation but led to a 23% rise in subsidy spending (Jan-March 2026). Structural reforms and free-trade agreements are expected to enhance economic resilience. Union Budget 2026 increased STT for F&O, but made share buybacks more tax-efficient. PROIs can now directly buy Indian stocks with increased limits.

items.headline: US stock markets rebound on strong Microsoft earnings
items.summary: US stock markets surged on July 30, with Nasdaq up 2.8%, S&P 500 up 1.7%, and Dow up 1.2%, driven by Microsoft's strong earnings and optimistic AI guidance.

items.headline: Asian markets mixed, chip stocks rally in Japan and Korea
items.summary: Asian markets showed mixed but generally positive momentum. Japan's Nikkei 225 jumped 4.64% and South Korea's Kospi soared over 14% due to chip stock rallies. Hong Kong's Hang Seng dipped 0.42%.

items.headline: Brent crude oil prices fall below $90, positive for India
items.summary: Brent crude oil prices fell 0.9% today, trading below $90 per barrel. This is favorable for India as a major oil importer, potentially easing inflationary pressures and supporting corporate profit margins.

items.headline: US Federal Reserve keeps interest rates unchanged
items.summary: The US Federal Reserve maintained interest rates at 3.50%-3.75% for the fifth consecutive meeting in July 2026, offering short-term relief and reducing pressure on capital outflows from emerging markets like India.

items.headline: Over 50 companies to announce Q1 FY27 results today
items.summary: Prominent companies like Bajaj Finserv, ITC, Maruti Suzuki, Sun Pharma, Indian Oil, ABB India, GAIL (India), and Shree Cement are scheduled to announce their Q1 FY27 results today (April-June 2026).

items.headline: Swiggy narrows Q1 FY27 net loss, Instamart breaks even
items.summary: Food delivery platform Swiggy narrowed its consolidated net loss to ₹791 crore in Q1 FY27 (from ₹1,197 crore year-ago) with revenue up 37.31% to ₹6,812 crore. Its quick commerce business, Instamart, achieved break-even contribution in May 2026.

items.headline: Vedanta reports 71.8% surge in Q1 net profit

items.headline: Tata Steel's Q1 net profit increases by 15%

items.headline: M&M Q1 net profit jumps 33.6%, Mahindra Last Mile Mobility achieves unicorn status
items.summary: Mahindra & Mahindra's consolidated net profit attributable to owners surged 33.6% year-on-year to ₹54.55 billion in Q1 FY27. Its step-down subsidiary, Mahindra Last Mile Mobility, reached unicorn status with a ₹10,822 crore valuation.

items.headline: TCI reports Q1 revenue growth despite slight profit decline

content.outlook: The Indian market closed marginally positive, with NIFTY 50 gaining 0.17%, primarily driven by robust FII inflows. Sectoral performance was bifurcated, seeing strong buying interest in Auto, Realty, and Financial Services, while the IT sector experienced significant selling pressure. This led to a mixed market breadth despite the overall index uptick and a low VIX at 11.8025.
keyTakeaways: NIFTY 50 and SENSEX closed marginally up, supported by FII buying.
Auto (+1.69%), Realty (+0.9%), and Financial Services (+0.8%) were top performing sectors.
IT sector saw significant declines, with NIFTY IT down 1.69% and major IT stocks among top losers.
FIIs recorded strong net buying of 3623.51cr, while DIIs were net sellers at 1864.03cr.
Market breadth was almost even (30 advances / 28 declines), reflecting mixed sentiment.
